layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose a method to decompose a video into a back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground and a set of foreground layers, where the background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captures stationary elements while the foreground layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capture moving objects along with their associated effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g. shadows and reflections). Our approach is designed for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unconstrained monocular videos, with an arbitrary camera

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and object motion. Prior work that tackles this problem

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assumes that the video can be mapped onto a fixed 2D can-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vas, severely limiting the possible space of camera motion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Instead, our method applies recent progress in monocular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: camera pose and depth estimation to create a full, RGBD

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video layer for the background, along with a video layer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for each foreground object. To solve the underconstrained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decomposition problem, we propose a new loss formulation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based on multi-view consistency. We test our method on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenging videos with complex camera motion and show

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signiicant qualitative improvement over current approaches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Decomposing a video into meaningful layers (as show in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1) is a long-standing and complex problem [42] that has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seen a recent surge in progress with the application of deep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neural networks [17,24, 25,46]. A challenging variant of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer decomposition is the omnimatte [25] task, which aims

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to separate an input video into a background and multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foreground layers, each containing an object of interest along

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with its correlated effects such as shadows and reflections,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thus enabling video editing applications such as object re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moval, background replacement and retiming. The original

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work on omnimatte [24,25] introduced a self-supervised ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proach for decomposing a video by assuming the background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be unwrapped onto a single static 2D background canvas

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using homography warping. Following work [17,46] relaxed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the homography restriction, but maintained the necessity of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unwrapping onto a 2D canvas.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This 2D modelling, however, limits the applicability of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these methods to camera motions that have limited or zero

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parallax; intuitively, only panning camera motions are al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowed. If the camera's center of projection moves a sig-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nificant distance over the video, 2D methods are unable to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learn an accurate background and are forced to place the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background detail in a foreground layer (Figure 2). Since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: camera parallax is quite common, 2D methods are severely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: restricted in practice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To handle camera parallax, we exploit another recent line

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 2. Existing methods fail on scenes with parallax. Top

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: row: Omnimatte [25] fails due to inaccurate homography regis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tration, reconstructing the majority of the video in the foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer. Middle row: Neural-Atlas [17] incorrectly places trees in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the foreground layer and struggles to inpaint the person region.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Bottom row: Our method obtains a clean background and captures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the person and their shadow in the foreground layer.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of work on estimating 3D camera position and depth maps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from casually-captured video with moving objects [18,26,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 48, 49]. Instead of a 2D layer decomposition, we propose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to learn a 3D background model that varies per-frame and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: includes inpainted RGB and depth in the regions occluded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by the foreground. Allowing the background to vary per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frame, rather than assuming a global, static canvas, creates an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ill-posed decomposition problem, as variation in each input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel could be explained by a foreground object, background,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or both. To resolve this ambiguity, we enforce that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background varies slowly over time with 3D multi-view

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constraints using dense depth and camera pose estimates [48].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As shown in Fig. 2, our model can successfully separate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers obtaining a clean background RGB whilst capturing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only the person and their shadow in the foreground layer.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Contributions. Our main contribution is a novel video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decomposition method capable of accurately separating an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input video with complex object and camera motion (e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parallax) into a background and object layers. To address

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the ill-posed decomposition problem, we design regulariza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion terms based on multi-view consistency and smoothness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: priors. The resulting model produces clean decompositions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of real-world videos where previous methods fail.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Layered video representations. There is a large body of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work on decomposing videos into layers based on appear-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ance and motion cues [4,8, 16,20,36, 42]. Layered video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representations have proven useful for a variety of appli-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cations, including view synthesis for static scenes [39, 50],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reflection removal [1, 2], segmentation [9], game decon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: struction [38], and text-based video editing [3]. Recently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Omnimatte [24,25] aimed to decompose a video into layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that group objects with their correlated effects, allowing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: user to perform editing tasks such as object removal and re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: timing. However, as discussed in Section 1, these works use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a constrained background model which limits their use case

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to panning camera motions only. Subsequent work [17, 46]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relaxes this assumption using general image warps, instead

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of homographies, but still cannot handle significant parallax;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moreover, their goal is to learn a per-frame mapping to global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sprites to enable applying consistent edits (e.g. style transfer)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rather than targeting object removal or video stabilization.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Monocular video depth. Multi-view stereo based meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods [23,40] incorporate motion estimation and multi-view re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: construction to predict depth by combining information from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiple reference frames. Hybrid depth methods combine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: single-view depth estimates from a pretrained network with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: geometric reasoning to obtain coherent depth predictions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With depth maps from monocular video as initialization,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these methods use correspondence to enforce consistency by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: either assuming static regions [26] or by modeling the scene

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flow [49]. Recent methods simultaneously estimate depth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maps and camera poses [19, 48], exploiting the depth prior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to resolve camera motion ambiguities. We rely on Casual-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM [48] to obtain camera poses and initial depth estimates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as their method performs well on casually captured video.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video completion and object removal. Patch-based meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods for video inpainting [7, 12, 14, 28, 43] complete the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: missing regions by borrowing pixels from other frames, rely-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing on correspondence estimated by homography or optical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flow. Learning-based works have explored the use of 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutions [5,41], attention mechanisms [21,30,47] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flow-based methods [10, 45] to achieve more realistic and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistent inpainting. These methods assume that the entire

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: region to inpaint is specified by an input mask, whereas our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method jointly learns where to inpaint the background while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: separating foreground objects and their correlated effects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NeRF for dynamic scenes. With the recent success of neu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ral fields [29,44] for view synthesis of static scenes, there has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been interest in their adoption for dynamic scenes [11,22,27].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These works learn two NeRF models that decompose a scene

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into a static and dynamic region. However, these methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only support a single foreground layer and do not account for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correlated effects such as shadows. ST-NeRF [15] proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to learn separate NeRFs for each person to obtain an editable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neural representation. Their method, however, requires each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frame in the video to be captured from 16 different view-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points simultaneously. Unlike NeRF methods, our method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represents the video with multi-layer mesh geometry where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object layers include associated effects, allowing editing as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as fast rerendering of the scene.

layout_dets.text: Figure 3. Model Overview. Given a frame from the video along with an input mask, disparity and known camera pose, we first extract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: networks. The background network predicts the inpainted background RGB and disparity. The foreground networks predict an RGB-A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Given an input video, with known camera poses and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initial depth estimates, the goal is to predict a per-frame

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer decomposition consisting of a background layer and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foreground layers encompassing objects of interest along

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with their associated effects. To this end, we propose a new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method that predicts a layered separation of an input video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without relying on a 2D background canvas, thereby allow-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing for greater flexibility of camera motion. We show an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overview of our model in Figure 3. We optimize our model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to output layers that reconstruct a single target video sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ject to a projection consistency loss. For each frame in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video, we estimate a layered representation consisting of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background and foreground object layers where the contents

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the object layers are conditioned on their corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input mask. Post-optimization, depth for foreground objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be extracted from the input depth to produce a Layered

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Depth Image (LDI). Unlike prior works that rely on deep pri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ors for inpainting the depth and color of occluded regions in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the background, our method relies on multi-view consistency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: losses to steer the inpainting process.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Data preprocessing. We perform our experiments on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 5. Discussion and Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We present a new method for layer decomposition that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: separates a monocular video into a background and several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object layers along with their associated effects. Unlike

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prior decomposition methods that rely on a static 2D back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground canvas, our method separates the video into layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on a per-frame basis, making it applicable to videos with un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constrained camera motion. To address the challenge of pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dicting a coherent background, we predict a 3D background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and propose a multi-view consistency loss that enforces the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background to only contain slowly moving or static details.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our model can produce per-frame Layered Depth Images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that allow for various depth-based editing applications.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A limitation of our method is shown in Figure 11. Unlike

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the background, foreground layers are not reprojected to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nearby frames and thus foreground objects are not inpainted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when occluded. This limitation could be addressed by adding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a projection consistency loss similar to Eq. (7) for the fore-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground layers; however, reprojection of dynamic elements is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenging and requires modelling the sceneflow, which we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leave for future work.
